context: One Identity spins out as independent company, relocates global HQ to Ireland

The company reports that its services are used by more than 6,000 enterprise customers and manage over 500 million identities.
It says that 80 of the Fortune 100 are customers and that its global partner network exceeds 1,000 organizations.
Fields Institute
The Fields Institute for Research in Mathematical Sciences is an independent nonprofit research centre with ties to 20 universities in Ontario.
Founded in 1992, it was initially based at the University of Waterloo before moving to the University of Toronto in 1995, where it occupies a purpose-built building on the St. George campus.
The institute is named after the Canadian mathematician John Charles Fields, whose name is also attached to the Fields Medal.

It brings together mathematicians from Canada and abroad and encourages collaboration with researchers in statistics, computer science, engineering, medicine, economics and other fields, alongside monthly meetings on mathematics education.

Sophos
Sophos is a British cybersecurity company that develops security software, hardware, and managed services.
Its offerings include endpoint protection, incident response, and managed detection and response.
Jan Hruska and Peter Lammer founded the company, which began making antivirus and encryption products in 1985.
During the late 1990s, Sophos concentrated on antivirus software and expanded internationally.
The business was listed on the London Stock Exchange before private equity firm Thoma Bravo completed its acquisition in March 2020.
In 2010, a majority interest in Sophos was sold to Apax Partners.
The company announced plans for a US$100 million London Stock Exchange flotation in June 2015 and completed its listing later that year.
ForgeRock
ForgeRock was an identity and access management software company headquartered in San Francisco.
Former Sun Microsystems employees founded it in Norway in February 2010 after Oracle acquired Sun.
They continued developing software that was otherwise due to be phased out in favor of Oracle products.
The company went public in September 2021, trading on the New York Stock Exchange as FORG.
Thoma Bravo completed its acquisition of ForgeRock for approximately $2.3 billion in August 2023, after which ForgeRock merged into Ping Identity.
Its platform included access management, identity management, directory services, and a gateway for web traffic and APIs, with components based on open-source projects including OpenAM and OpenIDM.
MaXware
MaXware was a Norwegian supplier of identity management, virtual directory and federation software, headquartered in Trondheim.
Its principal products were the Directory Synchronisation Engine and Virtual Directory Server, the latter designed for complex, high-volume environments.
The virtual directory brought identity information from separate applications and data stores into customized views for authentication and authorization.
The company had offices in the United States and United Kingdom, and SAP acquired it in May 2007.
MaXware's product history began in two Norwegian software businesses.
Former Norsk Data employees founded NOTIS AS after office-software development ended, while Televerket spun off its email and directory work into MaXware.
The firms merged in 1996, and the Virtual Directory Server originated in a 1995 project for Swedish Post's X.500 directory service.
Trellix
Trellix is a privately held cybersecurity company formed in 2022 from FireEye’s products business and McAfee Enterprise.
Its hardware, software and services support attack investigations, malware protection and assessments of IT security risks.
Symphony Technology Group bought FireEye’s name and products business for $1.2 billion in June 2021, then acquired McAfee Enterprise for $4 billion the following month.
The group combined the businesses under the Trellix name to provide extended detection and response services.
McAfee Enterprise’s security service edge operation remained separate, becoming Skyhigh Security.
In January 2025, Symphony Technology Group hired Vishal Rao to take over as CEO of Trellix.
At its inception in January 2022, Trellix had more than 40,000 customers.
The business focuses on threat detection and response using machine learning and automation.
Seamfix
Seamfix is a Nigerian technology company specializing in identity management, digital verification and software development.
Chimezie Emewulu and Chibuzor Onwurah founded it in October 2007, initially building custom software for local businesses.
The company later supplied SIM registration systems to telecommunications operators including Airtel, MTN Nigeria and Starcomms.
It also developed mobile enrollment platforms for Nigeria’s National Identity Management Commission and the Nigeria Inter-Bank Settlement System.
Seamfix expanded into other African markets and established offices in the United Kingdom and United Arab Emirates.
In 2024, it raised $4.5 million from Alitheia IDF to expand its infrastructure and digital identity services.
Qualys
Qualys is an American technology company based in Foster City, California, providing cloud security and compliance services.
Its QualysGuard software, launched in 2000, scanned corporate networks for vulnerabilities and looked for available patches.
The platform later added compliance tools, malware detection and web application scanning.
Qualys listed on Nasdaq under the symbol QLYS in September 2012, raising $87.5 million in net proceeds.
In 2015, it introduced a cloud platform and a lightweight agent for continuous monitoring of IT infrastructure and applications.
In November 2023, Qualys released Enterprise TruRisk Management software, which aggregates cyber risk signals to provide a risk-scoring framework for companies to measure and reduce IT risk.
In May 2024, Qualys launched a managed security services partner portal as part of its global partner program.
In March 2026, Qualys debuted Agent Val, an agentic AI tool for exploit validation and autonomous remediation.
SentinelOne
SentinelOne is an American cybersecurity company based in Mountain View, California, founded in 2013 by Tomer Weingarten, Almog Cohen and Ehud Shamir.
Its software uses machine learning to monitor computers, connected devices and cloud workloads.

The company completed its New York Stock Exchange flotation in June 2021, raising $1.2 billion and trading under the symbol S. It acquired the data analytics platform Scalyr in 2021 and the identity detection and response company Attivo Networks in 2022.
Tomer Weingarten serves as the company's CEO.
The company has approximately 2,800 employees and offices in Mountain View, Boston, Prague, Tokyo, and Tel Aviv.
In June 2019, SentinelOne received $120 million in a Series D funding round led by Insight Partners.
Since 2021, SentinelOne has been the official cybersecurity sponsor of the Aston Martin Cognizant F1 Team.

Okta is an identity and access management business headquartered in San Francisco.
Its cloud services handle user authentication and help developers add identity controls to applications, websites and connected devices.
The company’s single-sign-on service lets users access several systems through one login, and it also sells authentication services for application programming interfaces.
Todd McKinnon and Frederic Kerrest, formerly colleagues at Salesforce, founded the company as SaaSure in 2009.
They changed its name to Okta the following year, borrowing a meteorological term for cloud cover.
Okta’s services run on Amazon Web Services infrastructure, and the company held its initial public offering in 2017.
HackerOne

HackerOne is a cybersecurity company whose business centers on bug bounties and coordinated vulnerability disclosure, using outside researchers to find weaknesses in websites, applications and servers.
Jobert Abma and Michiel Prins began examining the security of 100 technology companies in 2011 and reported the flaws they found.
Their contact with Facebook’s security team brought them together with Alex Rice, and the three founded HackerOne with Merijn Terheggen in 2012.
By December 2022, its network had distributed more than $230 million in bounties.
Customers have included the United States departments of State and Defense, as well as GitHub, Google, Microsoft and PayPal.
Janrain
Janrain was a customer identity and profile management software company based in Portland, Oregon.
Larry Drebes founded it there in 2002, and its name referred to Portland’s wet January weather.
Drebes helped develop OpenID, a decentralized authentication protocol.
Janrain was a founding member of the OpenID Foundation and advocated the use of OpenID for online authentication.
Akamai acquired the company in January 2019.
Janrain raised US$3.25 million in December 2009 from DFJ Frontier, RPM Ventures and Anthem Venture Partners.
In August 2011 it announced a US$15.5 million funding round led by Emergence Capital Partners, bringing its reported funding total at that point to US$18.7 million.

Seraphic Security was founded in 2020 by chief executive Ilan Yeshua and chief technology officer Avihay Cohen.
Yeshua had previously served for many years as chief executive of the news website Walla.
The company’s browser-security platform protects access to SaaS and private web applications on both managed and personal devices.
It works across browsers and also supports desktop applications such as Teams, Slack, Discord and WhatsApp.
At the time of its Series A funding announcement, Seraphic employed more than fifty people.
A January 2025 funding round provided $29 million in Series A investment led by GreatPoint Ventures, with participation from several existing backers.
The browser-security company reported more than 50 employees and a threefold year-on-year increase in annual recurring revenue.
Its software also covered SaaS applications and desktop services such as Teams and Slack without requiring a virtual desktop infrastructure.
IDEMIA
Idemia is a French technology company headquartered in Courbevoie that supplies identity-security services, facial recognition systems and other biometric products to businesses and governments.
It was formed through the combination of Oberthur Technologies and Safran Identity & Security, also known as Morpho, following a transaction completed on May 31, 2017.
The combined identity and security business initially used the name OT-Morpho before adopting Idemia on September 28.

Morpho’s origins reach back to Morpho Systèmes, founded in 1982 and absorbed by Sagem in 1993; the business subsequently operated under several names before becoming Safran Identity & Security in 2016.

Its portfolio also includes automated fingerprint identification systems, iris and finger-vein recognition, biometric terminals, electronic gates, identity cards, ePassports, payment cards and SIM cards.
SGNL
SGNL was founded in 2021 by product and engineering specialists whose previous employers included Google, Okta and Microsoft.

The company develops identity and access controls for enterprises, helping them manage access to sensitive information and reduce the proliferation of roles across human users and non-human identities.
Founders Scott Kriz and Erik Gustavson previously built Bitium, which Google acquired in 2017.
They subsequently shifted their focus from authentication to controlling access to customer data, software code and cloud infrastructure using business context.
SGNL’s policies are designed to reduce the administrative burden of access management and address gaps in older privileged-access and identity-governance systems.
CrowdStrike to Acquire SGNL to Transform Identity Security for the AI Era
CrowdStrike announced an agreement to acquire SGNL on 8 January 2026.
The acquisition was intended to extend its Falcon security platform with controls that grant or revoke access according to changing risk.
Those controls cover human users, other non-human identities and AI agents, with dynamic authorization extending across software-as-a-service applications and hyperscaler cloud environments.
The transaction formed part of CrowdStrike’s Next-Gen Identity Security strategy.
The proposed deal was expected to close during the first quarter of CrowdStrike’s fiscal year 2027, subject to regulatory clearance.
SGNL’s technology was designed to re-evaluate access to cloud services and other applications as identity and device risks change.
ServiceNow to acquire Veza in major identity security play
ServiceNow announced plans to buy identity security company Veza and incorporate its access-management technology into the AI Control Tower.
Veza’s Access Graph maps permissions across people, machines and AI systems, allowing security teams to identify excessive access to company data and applications.
The proposed integration would combine those relationships with ServiceNow’s workflow and knowledge-graph tools to manage what AI agents can reach inside an organization.
Veza had about 230 employees and nearly 150 enterprise customers across industries including banking and hospitality.
The companies did not disclose the price, and the transaction remained dependent on regulatory clearance and other customary closing requirements.
CrowdStrike to Acquire Seraphic, Turning Any Browser into a Secure Enterprise Browser
CrowdStrike announced on 13 January 2026 that it had signed an agreement to acquire browser-security company Seraphic Security.
The company planned to combine Seraphic’s browser protection with endpoint data and threat intelligence from its Falcon platform, alongside SGNL’s continuous authorization technology.
The proposed combination was intended to provide a unified security system covering each stage of work, from the endpoint through browser sessions and into cloud services.

Chief executive George Kurtz said the approach would allow employees to keep using their preferred browsers while applying enterprise security controls, without requiring a change of browser or slowing their work.
Its security technology operates within Chrome, Edge, Safari and Firefox, including on unmanaged devices, without requiring a separate enterprise browser.
The planned integration would combine active browser-session telemetry with Falcon endpoint intelligence.
Okta acquires Axiom Security to enhance privileged access management
Okta signed an agreement to buy Axiom Security, an Israeli startup developing technology for privileged access management.
Founded in 2021, Axiom offers temporary access to critical infrastructure, permission-request and approval processes, and reviews of user access.
Okta planned to add these capabilities to its own privileged-access product over the months following the transaction.
The companies did not disclose financial terms, and Okta said it expected to complete the purchase in September, strengthening a platform intended to reduce unnecessary standing permissions.
The product announcement describes several specific controls: just-in-time access, automated request and approval workflows, and user access reviews.
Okta's chief technology officer said the acquisition would add connectors for infrastructure resources such as databases and Kubernetes.
The planned integration was intended to extend privileged-access controls to resources both on premises and in cloud environments.
The report noted that the financial terms were not disclosed and that Okta expected the transaction to complete in September.

How Scrappy Cryptominer CoreWeave Transformed Into the Multibillion-Dollar Backbone of the AI Boom

Richard Yoo, Dirk Elmendorf and Patrick Condon founded the business in 1996.
It grew out of Cymitar Technology Group, which Yoo started in a garage after leaving Trinity University to sell internet access to former classmates.
Graham Weston and Morris Miller supplied seed capital and began managing the company two years later, when it adopted the Rackspace name.

Xiaomi MiMo
MiMo is Xiaomi’s family of large language models, introduced in April 2025 with the seven-billion-parameter MiMo-7B.
The models emphasize mathematical reasoning and code generation, with training methods that include multi-token prediction and reinforcement learning.

The uncrewed Artemis I mission sent Orion into lunar orbit in 2022.
NASA describes Artemis as a sequence of increasingly difficult missions that use lunar exploration for scientific discovery and economic benefits while preparing for future crewed missions to Mars.

Seven missions launched to test optimised data transfer from space

Rover (space exploration)
A planetary rover is a mobile exploration vehicle designed to travel across the surface of a planet, moon or other celestial body.

Symphony
A symphony is an extended composition in Western classical music, usually written for orchestra.
By the late eighteenth century, the term generally described a work in several movements, often three or four, with the opening movement in sonata form.
A typical symphony uses strings, woodwind, brass, and percussion.
The complete score contains every instrumental part, while individual musicians read music written for their own instruments.
Some symphonies also include singers, as in Beethoven’s Ninth and Mahler’s Second, although vocal writing is not a requirement of the form.
The word symphony derives from the Greek symphōnía, meaning "agreement or concord of sound".
In late Greek and medieval theory, the word was used for consonance.

Underwriters received a 30-day option for up to 1,607,100 additional shares.
Trading was expected to begin on November 9, 2017 on the NASDAQ Global Select Market under APLS.
The offering was expected to close on November 13, 2017, subject to customary conditions.
Citigroup, J.P. Morgan and Evercore ISI were joint book-running managers.
The SEC declared the offering registration statement effective on November 8, 2017.
Apellis said it was offering all of the shares included in the IPO.
Matei Zaharia — education and early faculty positions
Matei Zaharia studied at the University of Waterloo from 2003 to 2007, earning a Bachelor of Mathematics in honours computer science with a minor in combinatorics and optimization.
He completed his computer science PhD at the University of California, Berkeley in 2013, advised by Scott Shenker and Ion Stoica.
He was an assistant professor of computer science at MIT from 2015 to 2016 before moving to Stanford in 2016.
His CV lists him as a cofounder and chief technologist of Databricks from 2013.
Zaharia created Apache Spark, an open-source engine for large-scale data processing.
His research spans distributed systems, cloud computing, and systems for machine learning.
He received the Association for Computing Machinery's doctoral dissertation award for his work on large-scale computing systems.
Peter Steinberger — document-software startup interview
Peter Steinberger described himself in a pre-WWDC19 interview as the founder and CEO of PSPDFKit, based in Vienna, Austria.
His background was in iOS development, and the document software began as an iOS product before expanding to Android, the web and other platforms.
PSPDFKit supplied document-viewing and interaction software as an SDK to other companies.
He said that arranging a visa for an early job in San Francisco had taken nine months.
In the interview, Steinberger explained that PSPDFKit supplies the document interface inside other apps, allowing users to open files, search their contents and select text.
He cited Dropbox as an example, along with software used in Lufthansa aircraft and by IBM.
The SDK is licensed to companies that embed document features in their own products rather than being sold only as a consumer app.
Clear Secure
Clear Secure is a biometrics technology company headquartered in New York City that operates identity and travel-document checks at airports and stadiums.
Founded in 2003, the company closed after entering bankruptcy in 2009.
Caryn Seidman-Becker and Ken Cornick bought the business in 2010 and relaunched it in 2012.
It went public on the New York Stock Exchange in 2021 as Clear Secure, using the ticker YOU.
Clear operates with the permission of partner airports, which receive commissions when customers sign up for new memberships.
Steven Brill and Ajay Amlani were Clear's original owners.
Clear received certification under the SAFETY Act from the United States Department of Homeland Security in June 2012.
Los Angeles International Airport receives 12.5% of Clear's revenue generated at the airport.
Centessa Pharmaceuticals — 2024 annual report
Centessa Pharmaceuticals reported 77 full-time employees at March 1, 2025; 36% held MD or PhD degrees.
Of that workforce, 49 worked in research and development and 28 in business development, finance, legal, general management and administration.
Its IPO registration statement became effective on May 27, 2021.
The June 2021 IPO involved 16,500,000 American Depositary Shares priced at $20 per ADS.
Each ADS represented one ordinary share, with a nominal value of £0.002 per ordinary share.
The 2024 annual report describes ORX750 as Centessa's most advanced OX2R agonist candidate and reports that its Phase 1 study produced positive data during the year.
By late 2024, the company had advanced ORX750 into the Phase 2a CRYSTAL-1 study for narcolepsy types 1 and 2 and idiopathic hypersomnia.
ORX142 and ORX489 remained follow-up OX2R agonists in IND-enabling studies for neurological, neurodegenerative and neuropsychiatric disorders.
Eoghan McCabe — autobiographical profile
Eoghan McCabe was born in Dublin, Ireland in 1984.
He studied computer science at Trinity College Dublin.
His early company, Eoghan McCabe Limited, became Contrast, an agency designing and developing web applications.
The team also created the crash-monitoring service Exceptional, which it sold to Jonathan Siegel in 2011.
He made his first website on Geocities in 1996.
At age 16, he worked in a local hotel bar clearing tables.
He subsequently learned to program at a local software company.
He built websites for small Irish businesses throughout college.
He began his computer science course in 2002.
He won the Ludgate Award for a final-year webcam face-tracking project.
Charlie Marsh — EuroRust 2024 speaker profile
Charlie Marsh founded Astral, a company that builds performance-focused tools for Python developers.
He wrote Ruff, a Python linter and formatter, as well as uv, a package manager, both implemented in Rust.
Before Astral, he worked at Khan Academy and later led a hybrid Rust-Python machine-learning and data platform as a staff engineer at Spring Discovery.
He received a Bachelor of Science in computer science from Princeton.
The EuroRust session description explains that the talk would examine the architecture and design choices behind uv, including allocators, concurrency and zero-copy techniques.

It framed Python packaging as a mature problem space shaped by specifications and tools developed over several decades, and asked how a new implementation could remain compatible while improving performance.
The event page reported that uv had passed ten million downloads per month after its February release.
Marsh's profile also connects his developer-tool work with earlier experience on mobile and web platforms at Khan Academy.
Arcellx — 2024 annual report
Arcellx was incorporated in Delaware in December 2014 as Encarta Therapeutics, Inc.
Its 2024 annual report placed the principal executive offices in Redwood City, California.
Its common stock traded as ACLX on the Nasdaq Global Select Market, with a par value of $0.001 per share.
At December 31, 2024, it had 163 full-time employees, including 112 engaged in research and development.
The filing describes a biotechnology business focused on immune-cell therapies and the development of candidates for serious diseases.
It discusses research, regulatory milestones, collaboration agreements and the uncertainty of clinical development.
The annual report covers the 2024 financial year and includes risk factors and audited financial statements.
